data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The dilemma dissolves if we view the preference as a 'conventionalist stratagem' that Popper ironically rehabilitates: we decide to treat the best-tested theory as true for the sake of argument, knowing it is not, to maximize the speed of falsification.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If acting on a theory implies believing it is true, violating the conjectural stance.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 'best-tested' theory is actually the most entrenched and resistant to new falsification attempts.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If this strategic view fails to explain why scientists feel confident in the theory's predictive power.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Popper's goal is rapid error elimination.
